chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Yazid al-Kunasī from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The muṭlaqah (freely divorced), the mukhayyarah (woman given choice of divorce), the mubāri'ah (mutual divorce), and the musta'marah (divorce by husband's request) — these do not inherit from their husbands anything during their waiting period (ʿiddah), because the bond of marriage has been severed between them and their husbands from that moment, so there is no return (rajʿah) for their husbands, and no inheritance between them.

key_terms.اَلرَّجْعَةُ: The husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period
key_terms.اَلْعِصْمَةُ: The bond of marriage / contractual tie
key_terms.اَلْمُبَارِئَةُ: A woman who initiates mutual divorce (mubāra'ah)
key_terms.اَلْمُخَيَّرَةُ: A woman given the choice to accept or reject a divorce
key_terms.اَلْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: A woman who divorces herself by paying compensation (khul')
key_terms.اَلْمُسْتَأْمَرَةُ: A woman divorced at the husband's request (istidrār)

ai.seo_question: Do different types of divorced women inherit from their husbands during the waiting period?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify that for *Khulʿ* (mutual divorce), *Iʿtirāʾ* (wife initiates separation), *Mubāraʾah* (mutual release), and *Mukhayyarah* (option of divorce), the marital bond is considered severed immediately, unlike in *Talaq al-Sunnah* where *Rajʿah* is possible. This immediate severance means these women do not inherit from their husbands during the *ʿIddah* period, a nuance critical to Shia jurisprudence regarding the precise moment of marital dissolution. The hadith underscores the principle that inheritance rights are contingent upon the continued existence of the marital contract at the time of death.
